analysis:
The PR changes only docs/developer/test.md. At base lines 958-960 it reworded the fixture-path sentence. At base lines 1085-1097 it replaced the 'Retained Console' section (make ui-* commands, Vitest/ESLint notes) with a short 'Console' section that says console tests run in the platform repository. No code, protocol, crypto, attestation, authorization, cache or key-handling behavior changes.

I checked the changes against the threat model. T-041 and the SSD cache material are in the surrounding unchanged test documentation and are not altered. The App Attest, endpoint-resumption and add-on hold test descriptions (TB-011, TB-012, T-053, T-059) are also untouched. Removing the console test instructions does not weaken any provider-side control. The model scopes the console and backend out of this repository ('Backend implementation, ... consumer console and admin UI' is out_of_scope), so this edit aligns the docs with that scope.

One observation, not a finding: the patch drops the sentence 'The retained console tests still read' and leaves the two wire-fixture paths with the verb 'are fixtures'. The result is a grammatically odd sentence and a slightly unclear fixture-ownership statement. That is a documentation-quality issue with no security impact.

No new attack surface and no invalidated assumptions. One thing I could not verify: the claim that the repository has no console test targets, CI lane or hooks. Whether console-ui tooling and its CI gates were actually removed elsewhere in the PR is outside the supplied units. If console code or CI were removed in the same PR, a later pass should check that no provider-relevant fixture parity checks (paged_footprint_wire.json, process_memory_wire.json) lost coverage.
